name: Competitor Extraction Eval Harness
introduction: An evaluation harness for one capability: extracting named competitors from a market document. Golden dataset, deterministic and LLM-judge grading, judge validation against hand scores, and a cost/quality frontier across model configurations, plus a published writeup. Success is not a passing score; success is a harness that catches a deliberately regressed prompt by a margin exceeding its measured noise floor. A vertical-slice spike has already run (writeup/spike-findings.md) and its measured results are load-bearing throughout.
goals: 50 labeled cases across five buckets, re-weighted toward where measurement is unstable
Three graders: schema and set (deterministic), judge (prose only)
Judge validated against 15 hand-scored cases, agreement reported as weighted kappa
Three configurations scored on a held-out test split with a cost/quality frontier
A measured noise floor, with the regression test gated on it
ownerRulings: R-1 PRIMARY MARKET ONLY: adjacent-segment competitors are excluded from expected, recorded in notes, and NOT added to must_not_include. Extracting one is an out-of-scope error, not a fabrication.
R-2 Buckets re-weighted toward empty/adversarial: 10 clean, 12 ambiguous, 15 adversarial, 10 empty, 3 long.
R-3 Manual steps are blocking gates in this file, not omissions.
manualGatePolicy: Stories with manual=true MUST NOT be implemented by an automated loop. The loop must halt at each gate and wait for the owner. A model-generated golden set, model-generated hand scores, or model-generated findings.md would void the artifact this project exists to produce.

userStories.title: [MANUAL GATE] Source and label 50 cases
userStories.description: As the owner, I need a golden dataset I personally adjudicated, because the labeling is the expertise and a model-generated golden set would void the artifact.
acceptanceCriteria: 50 cases: 10 clean, 12 ambiguous, 15 adversarial, 10 empty, 3 long
clean cases sourced from analyst comparisons or trade press, NOT 10-Ks
must_not_include populated on at least 25 cases
Every judgment call logged in notes; R-1 applied to multi-segment filers
At least 10 cases labeled cold (no model assistance) to measure anchoring
Cold-vs-adjudicated disagreement rate recorded
Split committed: 15 dev / 35 test
HALT: an automated loop must not label cases

userStories.title: Model-assisted pre-labeling CLI
userStories.description: As the owner, I want a tool that proposes candidates for me to accept or reject, so labeling is faster and catches names I would miss by reading.
acceptanceCriteria: python -m src.cli prelabel --case <id> shows each candidate with its evidence span
Accepts y / n / ? (defer) per candidate and writes to the case file
Records per-case adjudication time to results/labeling_cost.jsonl
Pre-labeling provenance recorded on each case so it can be disclosed
Unit test on a fixture case

userStories.title: Config loader and four YAML configs
userStories.description: As a developer, I want configs to carry model, effort, structured-output flag, and pinned pricing so runs are reproducible and cost charts regenerate identically.
acceptanceCriteria: configs/{baseline,structured,cheaper,regressed}.yaml load into RunConfig
Each pins model ID, effort, structured_output, prompt path, and price table
structured uses output_config.format; baseline uses prompt-instructed JSON
cheaper targets claude-haiku-4-5 at its own pricing
regressed equals the structured prompt with exclusion criteria deleted
Round-trip test asserts loaded values match the YAML

userStories.title: Set grader unit tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the set grader tested, because it silently lies when normalization is wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: Normalization: 'Dell Technologies Inc.' equals 'Dell'; 'HPE' equals 'Hewlett Packard Enterprise'
Near-miss returns a third outcome, not a false positive, at ratio >= 0.85
must_not_include hits tracked separately from false positives
Exact and near-verbatim (>= 0.95) evidence graded as distinct outcomes
Regression test for the mid-phrase-quote case found in the spike
Regression test for pagination-artifact normalization

userStories.title: Schema grader unit tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to know not just whether JSON parsed but how it was recovered, because the fallback path is load-bearing and intermittent.
acceptanceCriteria: direct / fence / regex / failed parse paths each covered
Over-length evidence (>25 words) fails validation and is reported
Confidence enum violations rejected
Test asserts parse method is recorded, not just validity

userStories.title: Judge grader for prose only
userStories.description: As a developer, I want an LLM judge with a validated rubric that grades only what a rule cannot.
acceptanceCriteria: Grades summary and evidence quality only, never the competitor set
Rubric scores faithfulness / relevance / concision 1-5 with a worked example per level
Requires reasoning before score, in that order
3 calls per case, median taken. Do NOT set temperature: it is removed on current models and returns 400
Document placed first with a cache_control breakpoint
Test asserts cache_read_input_tokens > 0 on calls 2 and 3
Median-of-3 unit test on synthetic scores

userStories.title: Metrics with bucket breakout and bootstrap CIs
userStories.description: As the owner, I need every metric broken out by bucket with confidence intervals, because an aggregate that hides a bucket failure is a false assurance.
acceptanceCriteria: Precision, recall, F1, must_not_include rate, schema validity, verbatim rate
Every metric broken out by bucket; no aggregate reported without its breakout
Bootstrap 95% CI (1,000 resamples) on every F1
Cost and p50/p95 latency per config
Known-input test asserts CI bounds are stable

userStories.title: Noise-floor measurement as a first-class run mode
userStories.description: As the owner, I need the run-to-run floor measured on the real dev split, because a regression is only real if it exceeds it.
acceptanceCriteria: python -m src.cli noise --config baseline --replicates 3 runs on the dev split
Reports per-case and macro-F1 spread and stdev
Writes results/noise_floor.json consumed by US-010
Generalizes scripts/variance.py, which currently hardcodes baseline

userStories.title: Report generation with two charts
userStories.description: As the owner, I want a markdown report and exactly two charts, so the deliverable is a frontier rather than a winner.
acceptanceCriteria: Markdown report: metrics by bucket by config, with CIs
Chart 1: F1 by bucket by config with CI bars
Chart 2: cost vs F1 frontier
Exactly two charts, matplotlib only
Any coverage the run drops (top-N, sampling, retries) is logged, not silent

userStories.title: Regression test gated on the measured noise floor
userStories.description: As the owner, I need proof the harness catches a regression. This is the acceptance criterion the whole project exists for.
acceptanceCriteria: pytest tests/test_regression.py compares baseline vs regressed on the dev split
Asserts the precision drop exceeds noise_floor x 2 from results/noise_floor.json
Runs fully offline from the committed dev-split cache, no API key required
Fails loudly if the cache is missing rather than silently calling the API

userStories.title: CLI
userStories.description: As a developer, I want one entry point for every operation so the repo is reproducible from a clean clone.
acceptanceCriteria: run, grade, report, noise, prelabel subcommands
python -m src.cli run --config configs/baseline.yaml works from a clean clone
--no-cache and --split {dev,test} flags
End-to-end test on cached fixtures

userStories.title: README and committed cache
userStories.description: As a reader, I want to verify the harness works in 30 seconds without signing up for anything.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce section is exactly three commands
Dev-split response cache committed so pytest runs offline in seconds
Documents that results are JSONL and the run-to-run diff is the regression signal
States the measured noise floor and what it means for interpreting deltas

userStories.title: [MANUAL GATE] Hand-score 15 cases and report judge agreement
userStories.description: As the owner, I must hand-score the judge's cases myself, because the entire point of validation is that a human disagreed at a measurable rate.
acceptanceCriteria: 15 cases hand-scored on all three rubric axes before seeing judge output
Agreement reported as quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa, plus exact and +/-1 rates
If agreement is under 80%, the rubric is revised, not the model
HALT: an automated loop must not hand-score

userStories.title: Score three configs on the held-out test split
userStories.description: As the owner, I want the three configurations scored once on held-out data, and the spike's variance prediction explicitly tested.
acceptanceCriteria: baseline, structured, and cheaper run on the 35-case test split
Results committed as timestamped JSONL
A second run produces a readable diff
Test split touched exactly twice total across the project
Explicitly tests the spike prediction: does structured collapse the variance concentrated in empty/adversarial?

userStories.title: [MANUAL GATE] Write findings.md
userStories.description: As the owner, I must write this myself. The code is table stakes; the writeup is what a hiring manager reads, and generated prose fails at exactly the sections that matter.
acceptanceCriteria: Sections: question, task/definition, dataset, grader design, judge validation, results, what surprised me, what I would do at customer scale
Includes 'what this harness cannot tell you': sample size, source bias, single labeler, one capability
Discloses model-assisted pre-labeling and the cold-label disagreement rate
Reports the noise floor and the 17% first-pass label error plainly
1,200-2,000 words, practitioner tone
HALT: an automated loop must not write this

functionalRequirements: FR-1: The system must cache by SHA-256 of (document + prompt + model + params); re-running a scored config must make zero API calls.
FR-2: The system must run async with a concurrency cap and retry-with-backoff on 408/409/429/5xx.
FR-3: The dataset must be 50 cases: 10 clean, 12 ambiguous, 15 adversarial, 10 empty, 3 long.
FR-4: Every metric must be reported per bucket; no aggregate may be published without its breakout.
FR-5: The judge must never grade the competitor set, only summary and evidence quality.
FR-6: Evidence verbatim-ness must be graded deterministically, with exact and near-verbatim (>= 0.95) as distinct outcomes.
FR-7: The system must log the raw request and response for every API call.
FR-8: Configs must pin model ID and price table; results must record resolved model versions.
FR-9: The regression test must run offline from committed cache and be gated on the measured noise floor.
FR-10: Document ingestion must strip pagination artifacts before any grading.
FR-11: Out-of-scope-segment competitors must be recorded in notes and excluded from both expected and must_not_include (R-1).
nonGoals: The full agent loop, other agents, RAG retrieval quality, or any UI
A plugin system, abstraction layer, or support for a second task
Automating any of the three manual gates

patternsToFollow: Harden what the spike built; do not rebuild it
Deterministic properties go in deterministic graders; the judge grades prose only
Every grader records how it reached its answer, not just the answer
Spike-quality labels are provisional and must be re-adjudicated, never assumed correct
reusableComponents: RunConfig and the content-hash cache in src/runner.py
constraints: temperature / top_p / top_k are removed on current models and return 400. Judge variance comes from 3 plain calls, not sampling params.
No seed parameter exists. Non-determinism is measured, not eliminated.
Structured outputs make schema validity near-free; that asymmetry is a finding, not a bug to hide.
Measured spike baselines: $0.055/case, 98% verbatim, 0 hallucinations across 49 extractions, noise floor 0.40 at n=5.

implementationOrder.description: Pre-labeling CLI first -- it unblocks the owner's dataset work, which then runs in PARALLEL with phases 2-3.
Harness core: configs, grader tests, judge, metrics. Depends only on the 5 spike cases as fixtures, NOT on the 50-case dataset -- so it proceeds while the owner labels.
MANUAL GATE. Owner sources and labels 50 cases. May start any time from phase 1 onward and run alongside phases 2-3; everything after this point requires it.
Measure the noise floor on the real 15-case dev split. Requires US-001.
MANUAL GATE. Owner hand-scores 15 cases for judge validation. The loop halts here.
Regression proof gated on the measured floor, committed cache and README, then the held-out test-split run.
MANUAL GATE. Owner writes findings.md. The loop halts here.

successMetrics: Noise floor measured and published on the real dev split
US-010 passes: a deliberately regressed prompt is caught by a margin exceeding the noise floor
openQuestions: Where do clean cases come from now that 10-Ks are ruled out: analyst summaries, trade press, or vendor comparison pages? Affects US-001 sourcing time.
Does structured actually collapse the empty/adversarial variance? Testable in US-014; if it does not, the variance is model-level and the writeup's conclusion changes.
Is 3 replicates enough for a stable noise floor at n=15 dev, or does it need 5?
Should the long bucket (3 cases) survive at all, or fold into the others? Least differentiating, most expensive to label.
parallelismNote: US-001 (dataset labeling) is the critical path and is owner-only. Phases 2-3 depend only on the 5 spike cases as fixtures, so an automated loop should build the harness core WHILE the owner labels. Do not let the loop idle at the phase-4 gate with phases 2-3 unbuilt.
